entries.subject: Add validated on-demand firmware build workflow
entries.comment: Capoworks ECU adds a manual GitHub Actions workflow, Custom firmware build, that builds firmware for one selected board from the current master source. The request must supply a request_id of letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens, a board from the fixed list, and optionally a comma-separated list of opt-in modules. The workflow always includes the base modules fan, fuel_pump, gear_detector, tachometer, trip_odometer, and map_averaging, and rejects base modules, unknown or duplicate tokens, empty tokens, and over-long input. It rejects lua on hellen128 and shock_preload on boards other than core8, atlas, proteus_f4, proteus_f7, and proteus_h7. It also fails if the workflow's module list no longer matches the firmware module catalog. The build uses the repository's own compile script for the board, so the resulting binary and generated INI must be treated as one matching pair. Artifacts are retained for 14 days and include fome.bin, fome_update.srec when produced, the board INI when produced, and a manifest.json with SHA-256 hashes and the source commit. This is a build convenience only: it does not flash hardware, and a successful build is not engine or hardware validation.

entries.subject: fix: restore Frankenso config generation and Windows simulator build
entries.comment: Capoworks ECU restored Frankenso configuration generation: gen_config_board.sh now resolves the host-only module profile against the f407-discovery board metadata when the board directory is config/boards/frankenso, because Frankenso has no board.mk of its own. Config generation itself still uses the Frankenso board directory. Builders generating Frankenso configuration no longer need a manual workaround; no tune, flashing, or runtime behavior changes. The simulator's SleepExecutor batch-order test now casts its expected and actual callback counts to int for the firmwareError format, so the Windows simulator build compiles. This is a test-only change with no effect on simulator or ECU behavior.

entries.subject: ci: use bundled ARM binutils on hosted firmware builds
entries.comment: The hosted firmware build now links the bundled ARM objcopy and objdump into a temporary tools directory and adds it to the job PATH. This is CI-internal tooling setup; the documented local Core8 helper already uses the bundled ARM binutils, and no firmware, artifact, or user workflow changes.

entries.subject: ci: move software workflows to GitHub-hosted runners
entries.comment: The software workflows were moved from a self-hosted runner label to GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 runners, with Java 21 and build packages installed inside the job. This affects only how Capoworks CI jobs are executed; firmware behavior, artifacts for users, and local build instructions are unchanged.

entries.subject: test: cover six cylinder defaults and full engine capacity
entries.comment: Test-only change adding a 6-cylinder CI matrix entry and a unit-test default of 12; it does not change firmware defaults or user-facing behavior.

entries.subject: build: enable six cylinder fuel trim tables by default
entries.comment: Cylinder fuel trim is now default-on with capacity 6; FOME_CYLINDER_TRIM_COUNT is optional and defaults to 6. Engines with more than 6 cylinders must raise the count or omit the module.

entries.subject: feat: make cylinder fuel trims optional and sized per build
entries.comment: Cylinder fuel trim becomes an optional build module with one 16x16 factor table per configured cylinder, a dedicated 1-to-12 count, all six load coordinates, shared axes, and materialized TunerStudio tables. Enabling it or changing its count changes the persistent layout with no binary migration.

entries.subject: docs: describe MCU resource budgets and validation limits
entries.comment: Documents MCU resource budgets: Lua heap sizes per MCU, F4 SRAM/CCM placement, 16 KiB DEFLATE dictionary, and F7 4-byte alignment, noting these are compile-time defaults and not validated hardware margins.

entries.subject: build: set module defaults and forbid Lua on Hellen128
entries.comment: Default module profile now includes boost, engine_sniffer, lua, and cylinder_fuel_trim, omits hella_opst, emp_pump, and shock_preload, and removes lua on hellen128. Explicitly selecting lua on hellen128 is a Make error.

entries.subject: Build: keep shock preload opt-in by default
entries.comment: Shock preload is excluded from the default module profile and must be selected explicitly with FOME_MODULES.

entries.subject: feat: port shock preload as an optional build module
entries.comment: Adds an optional Caponord electronic shock preload controller on CAN2 with preset, position, target, alarm and current telemetry, service controls, and a default-off enableShockPreload setting. CAN read and write must be enabled.

entries.subject: Build: keep native EMP pump opt-in by default
entries.comment: The EMP pump is excluded from the default module profile and must be selected explicitly with FOME_MODULES.

entries.subject: feat: port EMP pump as an optional build module
entries.comment: Adds an optional EMP coolant pump module with Caponord J1939 state machine, configuration and fallback tables, telemetry, service controls, after-run power hold, and CAN TX-thread queue. It is disabled at runtime by enableEmpPump and requires the fan module.

entries.subject: feat: make Lua code, tune data and editor schema optional
entries.comment: Lua becomes a build module; when not selected its VM, tune fields, gauges, bench outputs, and digital inputs are omitted. The console Lua editor now resolves the luaScript field from the active INI and rejects mismatched signatures or oversized scripts.

entries.subject: feat: make the Engine Sniffer recorder optional
entries.comment: The Engine Sniffer event recorder becomes an optional build module; the binary tooth logger and verbose trigger logging remain available without it.

entries.subject: feat: make Boost code and tune layout optional
entries.comment: Boost control becomes an optional build module covering its configuration, tables, telemetry, Lua hooks, and TunerStudio controls. Overboost fuel cut and the generic DC/ETB wastegate path remain available without it.

entries.subject: Build: keep Hella OPS-T opt-in by default
entries.comment: Hella OPS+T is excluded from the default module profile, so it must be selected explicitly with FOME_MODULES.

entries.subject: feat: make Hella OPS-T support optional at build time
entries.comment: Hella OPS+T support becomes an optional build module. When selected it provides the combined oil pressure and temperature sensor input; existing providers keep priority. It is not in the default profile.

entries.subject: feat: compose persistent tables and contextual tuner fragments
entries.comment: Modules can now contribute persistent calibration tables and contextual TunerStudio fragments. Builders adding module fragments must use the documented anchors and named INI contexts; malformed or misplaced markers fail generation.

entries.subject: feat: omit unselected module usages from packed telemetry
entries.comment: Build-time generator change that omits unselected module telemetry; no separate user-facing behavior beyond the module-profile documentation already covered.

entries.subject: feat: add static module composition and persistent layout identity
entries.comment: Tune images now carry a static configuration-layout identity. Binary tunes with an incompatible layout are rejected and defaults restored; export and re-import values with matching definitions because binary migration is not provided. Module selection is compile-time via FOME_MODULES.

entries.subject: Build: size Ethernet TCP buffers to the interface MTU
entries.comment: Ethernet TCP MSS is now fixed at 1460 bytes for a standard 1500-byte MTU instead of scaling with the TunerStudio block size. No hardware testing was performed.

entries.subject: Build: preserve F429 Ethernet main-loop placement
entries.comment: Only non-Ethernet STM32F429 builds move the main loop to ordinary SRAM; Ethernet-console F429 builds keep the main loop in CCM. This refines the earlier F429 memory-placement note.

entries.subject: Build: improve embedded INI compression density
entries.comment: Host-side compression tuning (memLevel) changes only build-time output density, not the decoder window or firmware behavior.

entries.subject: docs: clarify MCU memory placement and alignment
entries.comment: Comment-only clarification of MCU memory placement and alignment wording; no firmware behavior or user action changes.

entries.subject: Build: balance F429 main-loop and Lua memory
entries.comment: On STM32F429 the main loop moves to ordinary SRAM and the non-Ethernet Lua heap drops from 65,000 to 60,000 bytes; the 25,000-byte Ethernet heap is unchanged. F407 keeps its main loop in CCM. Timing and smaller-heap behavior are unvalidated.

entries.subject: Build: restore firmware memory budgets and deduplicate CI
entries.comment: F4 boards now place CAN, USB console, and USB mass-storage background objects in ordinary SRAM, and the F407 Lua heap drops from 30,000 to 20,000 bytes, reducing script capacity. The compressed INI drive uses a 16 KiB DEFLATE dictionary, saving 16 KiB RAM. F7 functions use 4-byte alignment. Hardware timing and smaller-heap behavior are unvalidated.

entries.subject: fix(docs): preserve README line endings
entries.comment: The commit only converts README.md line endings from CRLF to LF. The rendered text, links, tune format, build steps, and firmware behavior are unchanged, so no driver, tuner, installer, or builder action is required.

entries.subject: docs: link recent changes beside the wiki
entries.comment: The repository README gained a Recent changes link to the wiki. This is a documentation navigation change only; no firmware, tune format, flashing, or builder workflow is affected, so no wiki page needs updating.

entries.comment: Cylinder fuel trims now have separate 16 by 16 Speed Density (MAP/RPM) and Alpha-N (TPS/RPM) tables with neutral defaults. Layout 20032 resets older binary tunes, so back up the old tune and transfer former 4 by 4 trim values manually; Core8 also trades Lua heap space for the larger tables.

entries.comment: A new SD + Alpha-N fuel strategy can blend the two branch air-mass calculations through a TPS or measured-MAP authority table. The selectors do not change either branch calibration, and branch health, fallback and diagnostics determine when a blended result is available.

entries.comment: Independent captured load selectors let individual fuel, ignition and actuator consumers choose measured MAP, effective MAP, TPS, accelerator pedal or cylinder filling. entries.comment: Experimental time-budget dwell planning can retarget individual-coil ignition events within causal timing and physical dwell limits on supported synchronized triggers. It is opt-in, Legacy remains the default and fallback, and the behavior requires timing and dwell validation on the intended hardware.

entries.comment: Experimental cycle-profile timing converts ignition charge and firing angles using recent tooth history on supported missing-tooth wheels with full cam synchronization. It is opt-in and falls back to RPM-based conversion outside a valid profile; RPM and injection scheduling are unchanged.

entries.subject: feat(idle): add optional rolling-cycle RPM feedback
entries.comment: Closed-loop idle air and idle ignition can opt into a full-engine-cycle RPM estimate instead of instantaneous RPM. History must refill after synchronization or trigger changes, fallback behavior differs between the air and timing controllers, and idle PID gains may need retuning.
